From: Sam Lee <sam.lee@brightlinehealth.com>

Date: 2027-05-02T09:13:00-07:00
Subject: KPI & Observability Qs for Procurement - Brightline Health

Hi Rafael / Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — procurement asked us to capture a short set of questions so they can finalize the vendor review. We're primarily focused on SLO measurement, monitoring access, and the exception/credit path. Can you confirm the following? If any item needs a short diagram or a doc, please attach.

1) SLO definitions: how do you define "uptime" (per-region? per-route?), and what measurement window and granularity do you use (rolling 30d, calendar month, per-minute sampling)?
2) Latency: which latency metrics do you publish (p50/p95/p99)? Are these measured at application request level or token-level? Do you include model cold-starts in P99?
3) Monitoring stack: which telemetry is available (Prometheus, OpenTelemetry traces, Grafana dashboards)? Are there pre-built customer views or do you provide read-only links?
4) Alerting / escalation: what alerts do you have to catch SLO degradations vs. infra outages? What is the customer-facing escalation path and SLA credits process?
5) Retention & evidence: how long do you retain raw metrics, traces, and audit logs? Can we export metric slices for an audit?
6) Access options: for hosted vs dedicated vs private, what are the recommended patterns for giving read-only visibility? Any special networking steps (VPC peering, IP allowlist)?

We'd like short, concrete answers we can include in the procurement packet. Thanks — if it's easier, a 30-min follow-up is fine.

Best,
Sam
Sam Lee
Procurement, Brightline Health

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@brightlinehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-03T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: KPI & Observability Qs for Procurement - Brightline Health

Hi Sam — thanks, and great questions. Below are concise answers tailored for your procurement packet. I've attached a short definitions doc and an access checklist. Happy to jump on a call if you want walkthroughs.

1) SLO definitions and measurement windows
- Uptime: measured per-region and per-model-route (we expose per-route availability).
- Window: rolling 30-day window by default for internal alerts; calendar-month windows are available for contractual SLA calculations.
- Granularity: 1-minute sampling from our request stream; we also maintain 5s event logs for incident reconstruction.

2) Latency metrics
- Published: p50, p95, p99, and p999 for generation requests (end-to-end request time).
- Measurement: measured at the API request boundary (application-level); token-level breakdowns are available as supplemental metrics when requested.
- Cold-starts: cold-starts are excluded from contractual P99 calculations for Dedicated and Private customers if using pinned capacity; for hosted plans, cold-starts are included but make up <0.1% of requests for typical workloads. We document exclusion criteria in the attached PDF.

3) Monitoring stack and customer views
- Stack: OpenTelemetry + Prometheus (metrics) + Grafana (dashboards) + Jaeger for traces.
- Customer access: read-only Grafana views are provided for Dedicated and Private customers; hosted customers can request a curated customer view. For deep access we support time-limited Prometheus exports and archived metric dumps.
- We include per-route dashboards with request rate, success rate, latency histograms, KV cache hit rates, and model variant rollouts.

4) Alerting and escalation path
- Alerts: we run SLO-derived alerts (error budget burn, p99 latency threshold crossings) plus infra alerts (node health, GPU OOMs). Alerts are routed to our on-call and to customer escalation channels (PagerDuty or designated support emails).
- Escalation: submit a support ticket (support@redwood.ai) -> incident triage -> joint incident review for credits. SLA credit eligibility requires ticket creation within 48 hours and evidence export; full process documented in SLO_access_instructions.md.

5) Retention & evidence
- Metrics retention: 90 days hot metrics, 365 days aggregated rollups (configurable on Dedicated/Private).
- Traces: 30 days by default, exportable for audits.
- Audit logs: 13 months retention for enterprise tiers; SOC 2 reports available on request. We can provide metric slices as CSV for auditors.

6) Access options and networking
- Hosted: curated read-only Grafana + API-based metric exports (S3 export) via signed URLs.
- Dedicated: read-only Grafana and optional Prometheus federation; network via VPC peering or secure egress IP allowlist.
- Private/on-prem: full local observability stack with direct access.

Attachments: Redwood_SLO_Definitions.pdf (definitions + exclusion rules), SLO_access_instructions.md (steps for dashboards, exports, and evidence collection).

Next steps: I can share a pre-created Grafana invite for your team (read-only) and a short runbook for audit exports. Suggest a quick 30-min sync to walk through the dashboards.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_SLO_Definitions.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: SLO_access_instructions.md (markdown)]

Hi Sam — adding a few practical notes from the GTM side that procurement often asks for when reviewing access controls: 

- Customer access model: for hosted customers we usually provide a curated, read-only Grafana organization. This is tenant-scoped and cannot query other customers' metrics. For Dedicated customers we offer Grafana with Prometheus federation so you can point your own Grafana at our Prometheus endpoint (read-only, restricted by token).
- Networking: VPC peering is the common approach for Dedicated; for hosted we support customer IP allowlists and short-lived signed S3 exports for historical slices.
- Onboarding: we will provision two read-only logins for procurement/security reviewers during the contract review and rotate after onboarding.

I will provision a sample Grafana invite for your team for the walkthrough Rafael suggested. Proposed slots: Thu 5/6 at 10:00am PT or Fri 5/7 at 2:00pm PT. Which works?

Thanks,
Marissa
Principal Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: Internal: exception path & credit mechanics (internal note)

Rafael / Marissa — looping in a short internal note so we present consistent guidance to Brightline: 

- Credit mechanics: Credits are calculated on a per-contract basis; we convert minutes of downtime or error budget violation into a monetary credit per the MSA. For procurement, highlight that credits require: (1) ticket filed within 48 hours, (2) incident review, (3) reproduction window validation (we use 1min granularity).
- Long-tail latency: for customers with bursty or very long sequences we recommend an SLO addendum that calculates p99 over a 60-day rolling window and excludes extreme outliers beyond the 99.99th percentile — this is documented and must be agreed during contract negotiation.
- Evidence collection: Ops can provide Prometheus CSVs and trace exports; security can attest to retention windows. If Brightline requests SOC 2 artifacts, forward to compliance@redwood.ai (we'll redact internal-only fields).

I'll prepare a short PDF addendum with the exception examples (credit calc example, sample ticket template) and drop into the Drive link Rafael shared.

Karthik
Director of Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference
